title: Operator custodian handoff: SSO/KMS acceptance decision tree and sign‑off runbook
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Customers deploying Redwood Private require a clear, testable procedure to transfer operator privileges and cryptographic custody (KMS/HSM) from Redwood onboarding to customer operations without opening audit or control gaps. This ticket defines the acceptance decision tree, scope boundaries, and a concise sign-off runbook covering SSO/SAML federation, RBAC mapping, immutable audit logging, and KMS/HSM handoff scenarios (BYOK, escrow, emergency rotation).

Goal: Produce a single PRD-light artifact containing: 1) a decision tree to determine handoff path (managed keys vs customer-managed keys), 2) testable acceptance criteria for each path, 3) checklists for operational sign-off, and 4) links to artifacts (confluence runbooks, GitHub PRs, dashboards) required for go/no-go. This should be reviewable by security, infra, legal, and a sample customer operator.
scope_clarifications: In-scope: SAML federation setup and metadata exchange; RBAC role templates and attribute mapping; audit log retention and export for Private; KMS integration modes: Redwood-managed, BYOK, HSM-backed customer keys; operator credential transfer playbook.

Out-of-scope: Full UI onboarding flows for self-serve sign-up (separate UX project); long-term key escrow storage design beyond proof-of-concept; broad legal SLAs (handled as separate contract addendum).

Note: For air-gapped/on-prem customers, the runbook assumes an operator to operator handoff via a secure courier or out-of-band channel — acceptance criteria include documented chain-of-custody evidence and HSM quorum test logs.
decision_points: Is customer providing BYOK (Yes -> follow BYOK decision branch; No -> Redwood-managed KMS branch)
Does customer require HSM quorum for key unlocking (Yes -> schedule key ceremony & quorum test; No -> standard KMS rotation flow)
Is IdP capable of SAML metadata auto-refresh (Yes -> recommend SLO for rotation; No -> add manual metadata rotation step to runbook)
Does operator require delegated RBAC (Yes -> apply attribute-based mapping + scoped admin roles; No -> use baseline operator role)
Do audit logs need SIEM integration (Yes -> configure export + test ingest; No -> enable long-term retention exportable on demand)
acceptance_criteria: SSO/SAML: SAML federation validated end-to-end with a test IdP (Okta/ADFS/OneLogin). Test doc: 'saml-federation-e2e-OKTA.md' attached. Assertion attributes mapped to expected RBAC roles; automated metadata rotation test executed.

RBAC: Role matrix enforced in Private control plane: scoped admin, read-only, billing, operator. Attribute mapping unit test shows correct role assignments for 5 example users. No wildcards are present in operator role grants.

Audit logs: Immutable append-only audit stream enabled for all operator actions; logs exported to customer SIEM (or S3 bucket) and verified for retention policy (90 days default). Tamper-detection checksum present. SIEM ingest test (sum of event counts) passes for 72-hour window.

KMS/BYOK/HSM: Key material wrapping validated for BYOK case: key import logs, key policy binding to customer project, and HSM quorum test (3-of-5) documented. Emergency rotation run executed in staging without data loss.

Operator handoff evidence: Chain-of-custody document, signed access matrix, and recorded key ceremony artifacts uploaded to Confluence. At least one dry-run operator transfer completed with an internal sample customer (test tenant).

E2E runbook execution: Runbook steps executed in staging environment, with timestamps, PR numbers, and screenshots attached. Any deviations captured and remediated. Post-run checklist marked green by security, infra, and customer ops.

notes_and_risks: Risk: BYOK import failures could delay customer onboards; mitigation: provide a fallback Redwood-managed key path and document rollback steps.
Risk: Metadata rotation that is too aggressive can break IdP sync; mitigation: add staggered rotation with rollback window and notification hooks.
Note: For air-gapped customers, the key ceremony will require an additional approval from Legal and an offline transfer attestation.
